products.name: AirPods Pro 3
products.details: In-ear ANC and transparency, H2, Bluetooth 5.3. Apple claims up to 8h listening with ANC, 24h including case; heart-rate workout use up to 6.5h. IP57 earbuds and case.
products.limit: Apple features depend on supported hardware, software and region; non-Apple Bluetooth use is more limited. Fit and seal are personal. No generic Bluetooth lossless promise; official technical page does not list a codec inventory.

products.name: Sony WH-1000XM6/B
products.details: Black over-ear ANC model. Manufacturer: up to 30h music with ANC, 40h without; up to 24h calls with ANC. Multipoint, 3.5mm passive operation; SBC/AAC/LDAC/LC3 support.
products.limit: LDAC and LC3 require compatible source devices and settings. A codec logo is not a sound-quality result. The 30h music figure is not a 30h call claim; battery varies. No sweat/water rating was verified for this guide.

products.name: AirPods Max 2
products.details: Over-ear H2 model, 386.2 g before the 134.5 g Smart Case. Apple claims up to 20h ANC listening and supports lossless audio via USB-C.
products.limit: Heavier and more expensive than this shortlist’s earbuds. USB-C lossless is a wired feature; ordinary Bluetooth is not lossless. Advanced features need supported Apple software. No sport recommendation or water-rating claim.

products.name: Powerbeats Pro 2
products.details: Earhooks, volume rockers, ANC/transparency, H2, IPX4 earbuds and optional heart-rate sensing. Android app supports pairing and controls. Manufacturer advertises up to 10h buds / 45h with case.
products.limit: The headline maximum is not an ANC-on runtime guarantee. Larger case and earhooks deserve a fit check, including glasses. IPX4 is not swimming protection. Apple Vision Pro lossless claim does not imply lossless Bluetooth music from any phone.

products.name: Sony WH-CH520/B
products.details: Black on-ear model, SBC/AAC Bluetooth, multipoint, USB-C charging. Manufacturer advertises up to 50h playback; approximate weight 5.2 oz.
products.limit: No ANC or ambient mode; no passive wired input. USB-C charging does not mean USB-C audio. On-ear pressure and isolation depend on fit; no hands-on comfort verdict is claimed.

sections: A good seal changes bass and isolation in earbuds. Glasses and head shape change over-ear fit. Compare with music you know at matched, comfortable levels rather than treating “hi-res” as a listening verdict. Sony lists SBC, AAC, LDAC and LC3 for XM6; the source must support the chosen format. Apple says ordinary Bluetooth connections do not deliver lossless Apple Music. AirPods Max 2 supports a separate wired USB-C lossless path.
Calls: test the actual room and software

Shortlist microphone and switching features, then make a sample call using your usual meeting app. Quiet-room calls, a moving street and a busy café are different tests. Apple and Beats advertise Voice Isolation; Sony advertises microphone noise suppression. This guide has no recorded call samples or independent microphone rankings.

Sony XM6 combines over-ear ANC, a long claimed music runtime and passive 3.5mm playback. An airplane entertainment socket may still need an adapter. AirPods Pro is easier to pocket but depends on its battery and ear seal. AirPods Max 2 offers Apple integration and wired USB-C lossless, though weight and supported source connections deserve attention. Do not compare these battery figures as if tested under one protocol.

Powerbeats Pro 2 earns its shortlist place for earhooks and physical controls; AirPods Pro 3 offers a smaller alternative with a different fit and resistance rating. Both still need a real fit check. Water resistance is not waterproofing. Transparency mode is not a guarantee of hearing traffic or announcements; choose listening behavior appropriate to the surroundings.
Budget: spend on the missing feature

WH-CH520 covers basic Bluetooth music and calls at a much lower displayed price, with multipoint and long claimed playback. It omits ANC and wired fallback. If those are essential, saving for a different class may be more useful than buying a cheap model twice. The exact Black listing price is a dated observation, not a lasting discount promise.

PointCast / Shop / Research guides

POINTCAST / BUYING / LISTEN / OCT 05 2026

Headphones for music, calls and the rest of the day

Five exact configurations, chosen by routine rather than a universal “best.”

Compare the evidence ↓
How we reviewed

Research draft based on manufacturer listings and technical support documentation. Battery, ANC and microphone statements are manufacturer claims, not PointCast measurements. No listening sessions, comfort tests, call samples or independent rankings are invented. Prices checked October 5, 2026; features and results depend on firmware, source device and use.

Choose the headphone around your day: sealed earbuds for compact carry, over-ear ANC for travel, physical earhooks for sport, or a simple on-ear pair for a smaller budget. For an Apple-heavy routine, AirPods Pro 3 is the first configuration to examine. For mixed devices and longer over-ear listening, compare Sony’s WH-1000XM6. Neither is a universal sound-quality winner.

Music, calls and exercise impose different requirements. A microphone feature list cannot tell you how a voice sounds in wind, and an ANC claim cannot tell you whether the fit stays comfortable for a flight. Use the facts here to shortlist, then audition within a suitable return policy.
